paper_metadata.title: Quantum Monte Carlo Integration: The Full Advantage in Minimal Circuit Depth

experiments.description: Simulated univariate Fourier-QMCI benchmark estimating the mean of a 16-point probability distribution using Fourier decomposition and QPE-free quantum amplitude estimation, compared against classical MCI, rescaled QMCI, and conventional QMCI.

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate E(f(X)) for X sampled from a discrete probability distribution; in the numerical example f(x)=x.

problem_instance.description: 16-point univariate discrete probability distribution supported on {-8, -7, ..., 7}, encoded by a shallow state-preparation circuit.

dataset_specification.description: Probability distribution shown in Fig. 2(a); state prepared by circuit in Fig. 2(b) using H, Ry(pi/3), H.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulated results averaged over 500 runs; RMSE plotted versus number of uses of P.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct periodic piecewise extension of f(x), compute Fourier coefficients, allocate qn across Fourier modes.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Recombine individually estimated Fourier components to form the final mean estimate; fit RMSE scaling from simulation results.

results.unit: uses of P at the third data point
sequential uses of Q in a single circuit

classical_baselines.unit: root-mse slope implied by MSE Θ(q^-1)

speedup_claims.conditions: assuming QAE with λ = 2 and Fourier coefficients are symbolically computable; MSE scales as Θ(q^-λ) with q uses of the state-preparation circuit P
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports empirical RMSE slope -1.02 for Fourier QMCI on a 16-point synthetic distribution; constant factor is larger than conventional QMCI (194 vs 107).

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Theta(q^-lambda) MSE in terms of uses of the state-preparation circuit P; quadratic advantage when lambda=2.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Theta(q^-1) MSE for classical Monte Carlo integration.
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: 1100 uses of P at the third data point; 8 sequential uses of Q in a single circuit

experiments.description: Simulated comparison of conventional QMCI with quantum arithmetic for the same 16-point univariate distribution and mean-estimation task.

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate E(f(X)) for X sampled from a discrete probability distribution; in the numerical example f(x)=x.

problem_instance.description: Same 16-point univariate discrete probability distribution used for the Fourier-QMCI benchmark.

dataset_specification.description: Probability distribution shown in Fig. 2(a); state prepared by circuit in Fig. 2(b).

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulated results averaged over 500 runs; RMSE plotted versus number of uses of P.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Quantum arithmetic circuits would be required to implement the function mapping for mean estimation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Recombine amplitude-estimation outputs into RMSE curves; compare fitted scaling law.

classical_baselines.unit: root-mse slope implied by MSE Θ(q^-1)

speedup_claims.conditions: conventional QMCI with quantum arithmetic; asymptotically MSE Θ(q^-λ) and λ ≈ 1.05 in the numerical fit
speedup_claims.caveats: Requires quantum arithmetic circuits; paper notes this is depth-expensive and compares constant factor against Fourier QMCI.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Theta(q^-lambda) MSE in terms of uses of the state-preparation circuit P; lambda approximately 1.05 in the numerical fit.

experiments.description: Simulated rescaled QMCI benchmark for the same 16-point univariate distribution and mean-estimation task, using the shift-and-rescale approach from prior work.

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate E(X) via a rescaled trigonometric encoding of the distribution support.

problem_instance.description: Same 16-point univariate discrete probability distribution used for the Fourier-QMCI benchmark.

dataset_specification.description: Probability distribution shown in Fig. 2(a); state prepared by circuit in Fig. 2(b).

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulated results averaged over 500 runs; RMSE plotted versus number of uses of P.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Shift and rescale the support so that the trigonometric function is approximately linear over the support.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Recombine estimates into RMSE curves; compare fitted scaling law.

classical_baselines.unit: root-mse slope implied by MSE Θ(q^-1)

speedup_claims.conditions: rescaled QMCI using sin^2(x + π/4) ≈ x + 1/2 over the support
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper explicitly states this method has reduced convergence rate; numerical fit slope is -0.771, worse than Fourier QMCI.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Theta(q^-4/3) MSE in the cited prior method; numerical fit in this paper gives RMSE slope about -0.771.
